holdersRule: For every package that has at least one unit (an activated package), every OPEN occurrence of that package in the admission snapshot (checkedAtAdmission false and not since ticked by a unit tick receipt) must be held by exactly one unit, packet or deferral. A continued fold retains its launch facts and its state is re-projected onto the campaign store at remount bind, before any new frame; any non-continuing binding gets a fresh cell at EMPTY and does not re-show the retained fold. retainsLaunchFacts is kept. m13: the surface's refusal and projection helpers move to the new src/components/campaign/coop/campaignCoopSurfaceHelpers.ts, so the surface stays under the max-lines warning before binding grows it. Three surface suites register hand-built fake transports without campaignId (CampaignLifecycleGate, GuestProposalSurface, GuestRebuildStaleGate). Their fakes get the mounted campaignId, because connectStoredCampaignSyncTransport returns null for an existing transport whose campaignId differs from expectedCampaignId, so P2CG1G2's binding would otherwise detach them. hostProjection registers the P2CF2 m8 P1 case (rebind on a live bound transport) with the store behaviour. The consumer records a per-transport cursor watermark in heardAt when an active binding consumes any campaign frame, including a legacy frame, at consume without waiting for successful offer settlement. A rebind skips the new 60s pre-receipt window only while that recorded cursor equals transport.lastSeq(); a first frame missed while unmounted has no mark, and a sequenced frame advancing the cursor during an unmount gap makes the mark unequal, so either rebind arms the window. units.behavior: Both deploying co-op clients join the shared mission the server created. missionLaunchPage.launch.ts consumes the P1A-created, P1B-announced missionMatchId: the deploying host and the deploying guest navigate to and join the same tactical match, command-hq stays on /gameplay/campaigns/<id>, and the non-playing GM connection is preserved. No player browser receives or requests an opponent-control grant, and a guest disconnect grants nothing; this does not invent a guest-disconnect pause requirement, because PAIC/PAI preserve the existing host-disconnect pause rule. A failed or stale launch leaves both clients on their safe prior routes and creates no extra match. This unit also owns e2e/coop-campaign-two-browser-journey.spec.ts through task 1's node and unit path amendment: it adds the launch, deploy/HQ destination, shared match ID and active opponent-turn browser assertions to that journey and updates the spec's current no-mission-launch coverage comment to the behavior actually proved. Red-first: jest rows on missionLaunchPage.launch (deploy and HQ destinations, stale head, failed create) fail today because launch drops the composition before any shared match exists; the extended journey run through npm.cmd run verify:qc:coop-campaign-journey fails today at the shared-identity and opponent-turn assertions and passes locally and on exact main after. units.behavior: Every pull request prints its boundary delta, and the job cannot block a merge. A new pr-checks.yml job (the workflow runs on pull_request, :3-7) runs npm run qc:boundaries and prints the per-piece delta against the committed baseline. It is not in the Lint and Test aggregator's needs list (pr-checks.yml:700-721) and its gate step exits 0 unconditionally on the gate's own command line: the step's run is npm run qc:boundaries || true, so the step succeeds whatever the gate returns; the one other accepted form is an explicit set +e line before the command followed by a final exit 0. A bare trailing exit 0 line is not accepted: GitHub Actions runs a run step under bash -e on ubuntu-latest (bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail when shell: bash is set, as several pr-checks.yml steps do, e.g. :474), so a failing qc:boundaries line ends the step with exit 1 before a trailing exit 0 runs. continue-on-error is not used, because it lets the step exit 1 and only keeps the job from failing. The aggregator fails when any needed job's result is not success, skipped included (:725-736; analysis correction 28), so a report-only job inside it would block merges. Branch protection is unchanged. Until U66 is main-verified this job cannot fail on a grown baseline, so the parent checks each PR's baseline delta at review in that window, and any growth needs the owner's head-bound OWNER-RULING under sub-decision 8 (the decision's ledgerPlacement.reviewClasses). Red-first: a scripts/__tests__ jest pin parses pr-checks.yml (the yaml devDependency) and asserts that the job exists, is absent from lint-and-test.needs, and has a gate step whose qc:boundaries command is itself unconditional ('npm run qc:boundaries || true' on that line, or a set +e line before it and a final exit 0 line), with no continue-on-error on the step or the job; the pin's checker rejects a fixture step whose only guard is a bare trailing exit 0; red today (no job). Main proof, the analysis's Phase 1 exit criterion: qc:boundaries on the merge commit reports exactly the committed baseline (0 delta), and the job's delta shows on the unit PRs that follow.

units.behavior: The boundary gate blocks regressions. The gate exits 1 on any violation or runtime cycle not in the committed baseline, and on a baseline that gains an entry relative to the PR's merge base; a baseline entry whose violation is gone must be removed in the same PR (the baseline never carries a fixed edge). The pr-checks job joins the Lint and Test aggregator's needs (pr-checks.yml:700-721) and is never skipped (docs-only PRs take a no-op step, as prepare-build does). Its gate step drops U64's '|| true' (and any set +e or trailing exit 0), so the gate's exit code is the step's and a gate exit 1 fails the job; U64's exit-0 workflow pin is inverted in this unit. Baseline growth follows owner sub-decision 8: a PR that grows the baseline carries the owner's head-bound OWNER-RULING (a comment beginning OWNER-RULING <40-hex head> and the owner-ruled label); the job accepts growth only when both are on the PR for its current head and the ruling comment's author login equals the owner's login, pinned in the gate's config as SwiggitySwerve (the repository owner, and the author of all 14 packet rulings units.json records on f50e76fe4), and otherwise fails naming the decision. validate-roadmap.mjs:533-535 checks the label and the comment but no author; the job does not copy that gap. The login check refuses a ruling from any other account; it cannot tell the owner from an agent using the owner's gh credentials (the parent posts rulings the owner gives in chat under that account, with a disclosure), so that distinction stays with the parent's review, not the job. How the job sees a ruling posted after the push: the ruling can only be posted once the head exists, so the job's first run on a growing head fails. The job reads the PR's labels and comments live with gh when it runs (as validate-roadmap.mjs --github reads them; the job declares permissions contents: read and pull-requests: read), never from github.event.pull_request, whose labels are frozen at the triggering event and are replayed unchanged on a re-run. After the owner posts the comment and the label, the parent runs gh run rerun <run id> --failed, which re-runs the failed boundary job and the Lint and Test aggregator that failed with it; the re-run reads the ruling and passes. pull_request types stay [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review] (pr-checks.yml:7): adding 'labeled' would re-run every job of the workflow on each label event, and skipping the other jobs on those runs would fail the aggregator, which counts skipped as not success (:725-736). Red-first: scripts/__tests__ jest pins for a new upward import (fails), a baseline entry added without a ruling (fails), the same with a ruling for the head (passes), a ruling for an earlier head (fails), a ruling for the head posted by a login other than the pinned owner's (fails), a fixed entry left in the baseline (fails), and a docs-only PR (the no-op step succeeds); the ruling pins drive the gate's ruling reader through a stubbed gh, and a re-run pin calls the gate twice on one head with the ruling added between the calls (fails, then passes: the reader queries per run). A workflow pin, which replaces U64's exit-0 pin, parses pr-checks.yml and asserts that the boundary job is in lint-and-test.needs, reads no github.event.pull_request.labels, declares pull-requests: read, and has a gate step with no '|| true', no set +e and no continue-on-error on the step or the job, so a gate exit 1 fails the job. Main proof: the gate reports 0 delta on the merge commit.

units.behavior: LSC-2P finding F1, security half (owner decisions 2026-10-25 items 1, 2 and 6): the server decides who may save or delete a live co-op campaign record from the verified bearer, never from the request body. Today PUT /api/campaigns/[id] treats an envelope whose body.coopSession is {mode:"host", matchId} as the live host's own save (isLiveHostSave, [id].ts:141), so a guest profile that adopted the host-shaped record can overwrite it, the live host adopts the write and broadcasts it to the legitimate guest, and an anonymous DELETE answers 204 and removes the row. After this unit, while CampaignHostRegistry.liveEntryFor(id) holds a live host entry, PUT is accepted only when the request carries a bearer that verifies and whose principal is that entry's host, and DELETE is refused for everyone, the host's own included, until the session ends (owner ruling applied under the standing instruction; it changes the prep draft LW09); a member or guest bearer, an expired, malformed or absent bearer and a body-only coopSession are refused with a typed code and reason (HOST_SESSION_REQUIRED when there is no usable bearer, HOST_SESSION_EXPIRED when it expired; a verified non-host PUT keeps today's 409 live-coop-session conflict, owner decisions 2026-10-25b Q2 item 6), and the record, its version and the live host are untouched and nothing is broadcast. The host's browser store attaches its stored co-op bearer to record PUT; CampaignDashboardPage.tsx shows the server's refusal when Delete Campaign is refused while a session runs. The save-status card shows the server's refusal reason, keeps the unsaved changes and the dirty flag, and no longer labels a refusal "playing offline; changes are kept locally" (S4-03, refusal display only). Acceptance rows, each a failing test first: host same-tab reload (the bearer is still in sessionStorage) saves 200; host in a new window without the token is refused with the typed reason, the save card shows it and the unsaved changes are kept (disclosed: a new window cannot save a running co-op campaign, the host keeps its original window); app restart before any member reconnects (no live entry) takes the offline path and is accepted, pinned; app restart after a guest reconnected (entry live again) is refused as in the new-window row; expired host token takes the refresh path then 200, or a typed re-unlock refusal, never "kept locally"; offline host (no live entry): PUT and DELETE from another profile are accepted, pinned as disclosed behaviour so a later change is deliberate; a guest mirror save of its own record is unchanged; any DELETE while a host is live is refused, the host's own included, and works again after the session ends. Out of scope: the display half (a fresh profile rendering the HOST badge and host review surface), which owner decision 2 rewords out of Step 2 and discloses; record-scoped authority when the host is offline, the viewer-relative GET projection and the host re-authentication path, which stay with B15-3R and B15-3 after v2.2.0. The rule is keyed on the verified principal, not on a window or tab, so it does not preclude multi-window state for one identity (owner decision 6; MULTI-WINDOW-SESSION-1). It absorbs the host-save bearer attach and the live-host write rule of B15-2 and B15-3 by annotation only; neither is a predecessor.

findings.summary: The mission-launch page (src/pages-modules/gameplay/campaigns/missionLaunchPage.launch.ts:234-241, :311-318) and the dashboard launch (src/components/gameplay/pages/campaigns/dashboard/CampaignDashboardPage.launch.ts, which re-exports the same resolver) decide through resolveLaunchForces (src/lib/campaign/encounter/requestLaunchAuthority.ts:205-210). This is the documented pre-U20 client behaviour (requestLaunchAuthority.ts:196-204), not a regression. The nonClaim in evidence/u20-local-20260922.json that the client reads 'unavailable' and refuses the launch holds only for an 'unavailable' answer from the launch-authority POST (ownedForcesFromAuthority, :176-186), not for the head GET.
